definition:
Given a differentiable function $f(x)$ and a point $x = x_0$ on its domain, the tangent line (접선) to the graph of $f$ at the point $(x_0, f(x_0))$ is the unique straight line through that point whose slope (기울기) equals the derivative $f'(x_0)$. Because we already know one point and one slope, we can write the equation immediately using point-slope form (점-기울기 형태):

$$y - f(x_0) = f'(x_0)(x - x_0)$$

🗣 "y minus f of x-naught equals f-prime of x-naught, times the quantity x minus x-naught."

A closely related line is the normal line (법선) at the same point — the line perpendicular to the tangent line there. Since perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals of each other, the normal line's slope is

$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{f'(x_0)}, \quad f'(x_0) \neq 0$$

🗣 "The normal slope equals negative one over f-prime of x-naught."

{{graph:tangent-normal-perpendicular}}
workedExample:
Find the equation of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 2$ at $x_0 = 2$, and also state the slope of the normal line there.

Step 1 — Find the point of tangency by evaluating $f$ at $x_0$.

$$f(2) = 2^3 - 3(2) + 2 = 8 - 6 + 2 = 4$$

🗣 "f of two equals four."

So the tangent line must pass through the point $(2, 4)$.

Step 2 — Differentiate $f(x)$ to get the slope formula, then plug in $x_0 = 2$.

$$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 3 \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(2) = 3(4) - 3 = 9$$

🗣 "f-prime of two equals nine."

This $9$ is the actual slope of the curve — and therefore of the tangent line — at that single point.

Step 3 — Substitute the point $(2,4)$ and slope $m=9$ into point-slope form, then simplify.

$$y - 4 = 9(x - 2)$$

🗣 "y minus four equals nine times the quantity x minus two."

$$y = 9x - 14$$

🗣 "y equals nine x minus fourteen."

Step 4 — For the normal line at the same point, take the negative reciprocal of the tangent slope.

$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{9}$$

🗣 "The normal slope is negative one ninth."

So the tangent line is $y = 9x - 14$, and any line through $(2,4)$ with slope $-\frac{1}{9}$ would be its normal line.

{{graph:tangent-worked-example}}
teachingNote: A very common mistake is plugging $x_0$ into $f(x)$ and calling that the slope, or plugging $x_0$ into $f'(x)$ and calling that the $y$-coordinate. Remind students that two separate numbers are needed: $f(x_0)$ gives the point's height (used in point-slope form as $y_0$), while $f'(x_0)$ gives the slope. Mixing these up produces a line that looks plausible but passes through the wrong point or has the wrong steepness.
note:
📌 A tangent line (접선) to $y=f(x)$ at $x=x_0$ is the line through $(x_0, f(x_0))$ with slope $f'(x_0)$, found from $$y - f(x_0) = f'(x_0)(x-x_0)$$

🗣 "y minus f of x-naught equals f-prime of x-naught times x minus x-naught."

The normal line (법선) at the same point is perpendicular to it, with slope $-\dfrac{1}{f'(x_0)}$. New terms in this lesson: tangent line (접선), normal line (법선), slope (기울기), derivative (도함수), point-slope form (점-기울기 형태).

practice.prompt: What is the slope of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^2$ at $x = 3$?
practice.solution:
The slope of a tangent line equals the derivative at that point.

$$f'(x) = 2x \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(3) = 2(3) = 6$$

🗣 "f-prime of three equals six."

So the tangent slope is $6$.

practice.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 5$ at $x = 1$.
practice.solution:
Step 1 — Find the point of tangency.

$$f(1) = 1 - 4 + 5 = 2$$

🗣 "f of one equals two."

Step 2 — Differentiate and evaluate the slope.

$$f'(x) = 2x - 4 \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(1) = 2 - 4 = -2$$

🗣 "f-prime of one equals negative two."

Step 3 — Plug $(1,2)$ and $m=-2$ into point-slope form.

$$y - 2 = -2(x - 1) \quad\Rightarrow\quad y = -2x + 4$$

🗣 "y equals negative two x plus four."

practice.prompt: Find the slope of the normal line to $f(x) = x^3 + 1$ at $x = 1$. Give your answer as a fraction.
practice.solution:
Step 1 — Differentiate and evaluate the tangent slope at $x=1$.

$$f'(x) = 3x^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(1) = 3$$

🗣 "f-prime of one equals three."

Step 2 — Take the negative reciprocal for the normal line's slope.

$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{3}$$

🗣 "The normal slope is negative one third."

quiz.prompt: What is the slope of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^2$ at $x = -2$?
quiz.solution:
$$f'(x) = 2x \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(-2) = 2(-2) = -4$$

🗣 "f-prime of negative two equals negative four."

So the tangent slope is $-4$.

quiz.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 3$ at $x = 0$.
quiz.solution:
Step 1 — Find the point of tangency.

$$f(0) = 0 + 0 - 3 = -3$$

🗣 "f of zero equals negative three."

Step 2 — Differentiate and evaluate the slope.

$$f'(x) = 2x + 2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(0) = 2$$

🗣 "f-prime of zero equals two."

Step 3 — Plug $(0,-3)$ and $m=2$ into point-slope form.

$$y - (-3) = 2(x - 0) \quad\Rightarrow\quad y = 2x - 3$$

🗣 "y equals two x minus three."

quiz.prompt: Find the slope of the normal line to $f(x) = x^3 - 2x$ at $x = 1$.
quiz.solution:
Step 1 — Differentiate and evaluate the tangent slope at $x=1$.

$$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad f'(1) = 3 - 2 = 1$$

🗣 "f-prime of one equals one."

Step 2 — Take the negative reciprocal.

$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{1} = -1$$

🗣 "The normal slope is negative one."
